title: Tool Fallback Selection via Parameter Range Compatibility
description: Evaluates ordered fallback search with parameter-range checking against a no-fallback baseline on 4 synthetic tools with partially overlapping parameter domains.
novelty: Unlike the routing project (text→tool classification via TF-IDF/LR), this evaluates post-selection tool-use behavior: given an unavailable primary tool, the algorithm walks a fixed ordered fallback list and checks 3-D parameter range compatibility before committing, while the baseline fails immediately with no fallback logic.
method: Algorithm: for each task, if the primary tool is unavailable, iterate a fixed ordered fallback list of 3 alternatives; select the first fallback whose 3-D parameter range encloses the task's parameter vector; record the list position as depth. If no fallback accepts, the task fails. Baseline: no fallback—unavailable primary means immediate failure after 1 call. Data: n_samples tasks with columns [tool_id(0-3), p1, p2, p3, unavailable_flag]; params are sampled uniformly from the primary tool's range so the primary can always handle them; unavailability is a seeded Bernoulli(p=0.3) flag. y=1 if the task is completable (primary available OR at least one other tool's range contains the params), y=0 otherwise. No train/test split: each task is an independent deterministic evaluation and the algorithm must reproduce the ground-truth completability. Metrics (direction): completion_rate (higher=better, fraction of tasks the strategy completes), avg_tool_calls (lower=better, mean attempts per task including primary), mean_fallback_depth (lower=better, 0=primary used, 1-3=fallback position; baseline is always 0). Tool ranges are non-overlapping enough that ~5-15% of tasks are truly incompletable, making y non-trivial.
acceptance_tests: make_dataset(1, 64) returns X with shape (64, 5) and y with shape (64,); make_dataset(2, 64) returns an X that is not array-equal to the seed-1 X
run_experiment(42, 128) returns metrics['completion_rate'] >= baseline_metrics['completion_rate'], metrics['avg_tool_calls'] >= 1.0, and every value in metrics and baseline_metrics is finite
